question: An engineer configured an environment that contains the vPC and non-vPC switches. However, it was noticed that the downstream non-vPC switches do not receive the same STP bridge ID from the upstream vPC switch peers. Which vPC feature must be implemented to ensure that vPC and non-vPC switches receive the same STP bridge ID from the upstream vPC switch peers?
theory: Without "peer-switch," each vPC peer advertises its own individual bridge ID in BPDUs sent out non-vPC ports, so a downstream non-vPC switch dual-homed (via separate links) to both peers can see two different STP bridge IDs from what should look like one logical upstream switch. Enabling "peer-switch" makes both vPC peers advertise the same vPC-system bridge ID consistently on both vPC and non-vPC ports, so any downstream device — vPC-attached or not — sees a single, consistent STP root/bridge ID from the pair. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Peer-Switch)
